ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $l_{1}\parallel l_{2}\parallel l_{3}$. If $AB=2$, $BC=3$, $AD=1$, and $CF=4$, what is the length of $BE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Construct line $DN \parallel AC$ through point D to intersect $BE$ at point $M$, and $CF$ at point $N$;\\
$\therefore$ Quadrilaterals $ABMD$ and $BCNM$ are both parallelograms\\
$\therefore$ $AB=DM=2$,\\
$BC=MN=3$,\\
$AD=BM=CN=1$\\
From the problem, we know\\
$\frac{AB}{BC}=\frac{DE}{EF}=\frac{2}{3}$\\
$\because BE\parallel CF$\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle DME\sim \triangle DNF$\\
$\therefore$ $\frac{ME}{NF}=\frac{DE}{DF}=\frac{DM}{DN}=\frac{DM}{DM+MN}=\frac{2}{5}$\\
$\because NF=CF-CN=4-1=3$\\
$\therefore$ $ME=\frac{6}{5}$\\
$\therefore$ $BE=BM+ME=1+\frac{6}{5}=\boxed{\frac{11}{5}}$

method.method_draft: Set up coordinates from the picture. Treat the three parallel lines as horizontal. Put l1 at y=0 and l3 at y=1. From the image, A and D are on l1, B and E are on l2, C and F are on l3, with A,B,C collinear and D,E,F collinear. Let A=(0,0), D=(1,0) because AD=1. Let C=(u,1) and F=(u+4,1) because CF=4. Since AB:BC=2:3 on the same straight transversal, B is 2/5 of the way from A to C, so B=(2u/5, 2/5). The line l2 therefore has y=2/5. Point E is where the right transversal DF reaches y=2/5, so E = D + (2/5)(F-D) = (1 + (2/5)(u+3), 2/5). Thus BE is the horizontal distance between E and B: BE = [1 + (2/5)(u+3)] - 2u/5 = 1 + 6/5 = 11/5.
